page: Microsoft Azure M16-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, and a dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with an exceptionally high memory capacity of 438.0 GB, translating to 109.38 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the instance includes 524 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, while containing no GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the server prioritizes memory capacity over raw processing speed and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 1033.09 and multi-core score of 2722.46 fall into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 151.48 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 18.75 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both placing in the bottom 10%. Geekbench scores further confirm this profile, with a single-core score of 884.0 and a multi-core score of 1961.0. Database operations and key-value store performance are modest, with Redis SET operations reaching 2.69 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M16-4ms represents a highly specialized resource allocation. Users pay a premium for the massive memory footprint relative to the low vCPU count, making it inefficient for compute-heavy tasks but highly dense for memory-bound applications. The primary tradeoff is the low compute-to-memory ratio and lower memory bandwidth. This server is best suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications that require massive RAM capacity but have low parallel processing demands.
